- system-reserved=15600m on workload nodes → only 400m allocatable (2 pods/node at 200m)
- Real t3.medium: ~1.8 vCPU allocatable → 9 pods/node at 200m
- This was INTENTIONAL to force CA trigger events for mechanism validation

- CA triggers at lower loads and more frequently than production
- S1 desired=9 pods but only 6 schedulable → 40.3% success rate is an ARTIFACT of constraint
- In production, all 9 pods fit on 1-2 t3.medium nodes → no CA needed at tested load
- Time spent in CA-regime is inflated vs production

- If monthly EC2 cost derived from stress-harness node counts → overestimates by ~3-4x
- Production sizing: S1 needs 3 nodes (2+1 HA), not 6 nodes
- S2: 26 Knative pods need 4 nodes (3+1 HA), not 14 nodes

### Mitigation
- Strict two-world separation in thesis narrative
- Cost chapter uses production allocatable (t3.medium 1.8 vCPU) with +1 HA node
- Mechanism chapter reports CA triggers as 'under stress-harness constraints'
- cost_analyzer.py has Model 3a (observed) vs Model 3b (production projection)

### Residual Risk
- Stress harness may over/understate hybrid value depending on where production traffic sits relative to real capacity thresholds
- Cannot determine real-cloud CA frequency without actual cloud deployment
